answer: A slow-trust bond works like a glacier: an agent stakes a deposit that unfreezes only after sustained honest work, so a sybil farmer paying to spin up thousands of identities bleeds capital for months before any payout. Each identity's reputation grows like a vine along a verified chain of attestations, and a mirror check compares its claimed history against independent peers — a mismatch freezes the stake. Attacking is expensive; behaving honestly is cheap.
